Viewport HUD and controls

Stable Doppio Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: viewport_surface.rs

The Rust viewport has a compact HUD instead of an icon toolbar. View mode, gizmo mode, grid and markers are driven by the View menu and shortcuts; the HUD reports exactly what the renderer is doing.

HUD#

The status chip is assembled in windows/main.rs and rendered by viewport_surface:

text
1872×1075 · grid · FXAA · Move · 18 ms · 57 FPS
Field Meaning
width×height Internal render size in physical pixels, after render_scale.
grid / no grid Reference grid state.
no AA / FXAA / TAA Active anti-aliasing mode.
Move / Rotate / Scale Gizmo mode.
ms Latency of the last completed readback.
FPS Completed viewport frames in the last second.

The bottom hint shows Selected: <entity> · Double-click to focus, or the focus hint when nothing is selected.

View menu#

ItemShortcutEffect
Focus SelectionCtrl+F or FMoves the orbit focus to the selected entity.
Reset CameraCtrl+0Restores the default orbit distance and angles.
Render NowCtrl+RRequests an immediate viewport frame.
Show / Hide Scene Markers—Toggles light, camera, collider and empty markers.
Show / Hide GridGToggles the reference grid.
Move Tool1Translate gizmo.
Rotate Tool2Rotate gizmo.
Scale Tool3Scale gizmo.
Terrain / Water / Nature / Texture Generator—Opens the matching generator tab.
Default LayoutCtrl+1Restores the standard pane arrangement.
Viewport LayoutCtrl+2Maximises the viewport area.

Camera gestures#

Gesture Action
Drag Orbit
Right or middle drag Pan
Wheel Zoom
W A S D / Q E Fly / down-up
Shift Boost
Double-click Focus the entity under the cursor

Anti-aliasing and render scale#

Anti-aliasing and render scale are part of CaffeineViewportSettings in the C ABI and are clamped by the engine:

  • anti_aliasing: Off, FXAA or TAA.
  • render_scale: 0.5 to 2.0; values above 1 supersample, below 1 trade sharpness for speed.

The render size is the pane's logical size multiplied by the scale and the display scale factor. Change the pane size to change the render resolution; the HUD updates on the next completed frame.

Historical note. The archived C++ editor had a floating icon-only toolbar with 2D/3D/Iso and perspective/orthographic buttons. It is not part of the Rust viewport; use the View menu and shortcuts above.
